{{Quote|This is the ''Empirical'', master, Lord Vader's top-secret mobile laboratory.|PROXY, to Galen Marek|<ref name="TFUn" />}}
The '''ISS ''Empirical''''' was a mobile research [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]], a modified [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] that belonged to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Rumoured to be one of many such [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] used by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]], the ''Empirical'' housed the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg's]] experiments on [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]] and studies conducted on unique [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Top-secret, moving only between lifeless [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and escaping even the eyes of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] spy network, the vessel was crewed by a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] personally selected by [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader, who monitored the test subjects and eliminated those that escaped confinement before they could get off the ship. One of the many such experiments was [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Rom Mohc]]'s [[Dark Trooper Project|Dark Trooper Phase Zero project]], which operated out of the ''Empirical'' until it was shut down for practical reasons.

When Vader's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Galen Marek]] was injured close to [[Death/Legends|death]] on the orders of Palpatine, Vader brought him to the ''Empirical'' to be rehabilitated, bringing along Marek's ship, the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', and his [[Droid/Legends|droid]], [[PROXY]]. Vader later sent Marek's [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], to the vessel after she was arrested for [[Treason/Legends|treason]]. When Marek awoke after six months, PROXY helped him escape the vessel, kill many of the crew&mdash;who thought he was one of Vader's experiments and had orders to terminate him&mdash;and free Eclipse. Under orders from Vader to remove all evidence that Marek had been there, including the crew, PROXY disabled the ship's navigational systems and set it on a course into the [[Dominus system/Legends|Dominus system's]] primary [[Star/Legends|star]]. Marek, Eclipse, and PROXY escaped on the ''Rogue Shadow'' as the ''Empirical'' plunged into the star and exploded.

==Description==
The ISS ''Empirical'' was a mobile research [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]] owned by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]],<ref name="TFUn" /><ref name="TFUd" /> the [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Forces]].<ref name="kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Darth Vader vs. Prince Xizor|link=soteKxizor-vader.asp}}</ref> A modified [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]],<ref name="TFUn" /> the ''Empirical'' was rumored to be one of many similar research [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] in a fleet helmed by the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|right-hand]].<ref name="TFUd" /> The ''Empirical''{{'s}} purpose was to house [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader's experiments on [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]], as well as study unique [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="TFUd" /> The ship was propelled by five [[Engine/Legends|engines]], four in the stern and one mounted nearer the bow, on a spur of the ship emerging from its ventral side. It was armed with at least two [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]]. The vessel was equipped with at least six [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]], the room for which was accessible by [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] from other decks,<ref name="TFUg" /> and had a [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] suitable for berthing a [[Transport/Legends|transport]]-sized ship.<ref name="TFUc" /> The ship also had an intercom system that was operated by an [[Empirical announcer|announcer]] who reported updates on the ship's operations.<ref name="TFUn" />

The ''Empirical'' was a top-secret vessel;<ref name="TFUn" /> even [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] spy network could not track it. The vessel stuck to lifeless [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], traveling courses between them that had long been forgotten.<ref name="TFUd" />

===Medical and experimental facilities===
[[File:Empirical_Medbay.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A medical room of the ''Empirical''.]]
Fitting with its primary function, the ''Empirical'' had a number of rooms with testing and medical facilities. One such room, located in Sector Ten&mdash;the stern of the vessel between its engines&mdash;was used to hold [[Galen Marek]] during his recuperation aboard the ''Empirical''. Marek was kept restrained to a table inside a [[Glass/Legends|glassed]]-off portion of the room, where several [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] could operate on him. The room began piping in poisonous gas when Marek tried to escape, and the crew was alerted to the security breach. This same room held half a dozen similar operating tables, all of them empty at the time.<ref name="TFUg" />

A nearby room contained a number of chambers filled with a toxic gas. Surrounded by catwalks, it was monitored by several [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], including [[EVO trooper]]s, and watched over from a small observation room by an [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]].<ref name="TFUg" />

===Detention cells===
Detention cells were located near the bow of the vessel.<ref name="TFUg" /> The detainment area was large and difficult for soldiers to defend from an assault.<ref name="TFUn" /> [[Force field/Legends|Force fields]] could be thrown up to ward off attacks for a time, but they could be taken down by cutting the power.<ref name="TFUg" /> Prisoners were suspended in their cells by [[Magna lock/Legends|magna locks]]. Though they were usually left to die, those that Vader wanted kept alive were occasionally let down for short periods, in which they were allowed to use the [[Refresher/Legends|refresher]] and drink [[Water/Legends|water]], but not always eat.<ref name="TFUn" />

==History==
{{Quote|Check out that noise! I think Lord Vader's experiment just got loose.|A stormtrooper aboard the ''Empirical'', before being killed by Galen Marek|<ref name="TFUg" />}}
One of several projects conducted aboard the ''Empirical'' was the [[Dark Trooper Project|Dark Trooper Phase Zero project]], overseen by [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Rom Mohc]]. A way to supplement the Empire's troop shortage after the shutdown of the [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] facilities, the Phase Zero project involved taking aging [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] veterans of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and, using much of the same [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] technology involved in Lord Vader's own creation, converting them into [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborgs]] through the replacement of organs and limbs with cybernetics. Though moderately successful, the Phase Zero project was dismantled when the Empire's recruitment picked up.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:Empirical.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The ''Empirical'' nears the star of the Dominus system.]]
In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]], Emperor Palpatine confronted Lord Vader on the latter's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], over his taking of an apprentice, Galen Marek. To prove his loyalty, Vader [[Shiak|impaled]] Marek with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and cast him out into the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Secretly, however, a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] retrieved Marek's unconscious body and took him to the ''Empirical''. Vader's medical droids spent six months rebuilding Marek, as the apprentice lay unconscious.<ref name="TFUn" /> To the rest of the ship, Marek was viewed as another of Vader's experiments, and he was designated "Subject Zeta" and "Subject 1138."<ref name="TFUn" /><ref name="TFUg" /> Vader had Marek's droid [[PROXY]] and ship, the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', delivered to the vessel as well, and to aid in his mission Marek was given a new lightsaber.<ref name="TFUn" /> His pilot, [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], had meanwhile been arrested for treason; after some time, she too was transported to the ''Empirical'', where she feared she would become part of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith's]] experiments.<ref name="TFUg" />

[[File:Empirical_cell.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Galen Marek rescues Juno Eclipse.]]
When Marek at last awoke after six months, by which time the ''Empirical'' had moved into the [[Dominus system/Legends|Dominus system]], he was greeted by Vader, transmitting his image through PROXY. Vader told Marek that Palpatine believed him to be dead, then assigned him the task of building an [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|army]] to oppose Palpatine. The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] threatened to activate the ''Empirical''{{'s}} self-destruct sequence if his apprentice did not comply, but the latter gave in.<ref name="TFUn" /> PROXY, too, had been given instructions, and when Vader cut his transmission, the droid set about fulfilling his orders to help Marek escape, and to eliminate all evidence of Marek's survival, including the vessel and its crew.<ref name="TFUn" /> Marek broke out of his chamber, and his room began to flood with poison gas; he turned it off, but a squad was sent to monitor the situation. An alert was sent through the ship warning that Vader's subject had escaped. Having heard from PROXY that Eclipse was aboard, Marek went for her first, slaughtering his way through the crew, all of whom had orders to kill him. PROXY, meanwhile, accessed the vessel's main [[Computer/Legends|computer]], and, determining it was the quickest way to eliminate everyone aboard, set the ship on a course into the system's [[Star/Legends|star]]. The crew of the ship was alarmed when their navigation began malfunctioning, and a series of announcements apprised the rest of the vessel of the deteriorating situation. An evacuation was ordered, but PROXY continued with his work, disabling security systems and, to make sure no crew members made it out, ejecting the ship's escape pods.<ref name="TFUg" />

Marek made it to Eclipse's detention cell to find several of the ship's officers with her, behind a force field. After killing the stormtroopers outside it, Marek brought down the field, eliminated the rest of the crew in the vicinity, and rescued Eclipse from her restraints. He helped Eclipse get to the ''Rogue Shadow'', which PROXY had gotten ready, and they evacuated the research vessel. The ''Empirical'', meanwhile, continued on its doomed course, exploding as it fell into the system's sun.<ref name="TFUg" />

==Commanders and crew==
The ''Empirical''{{'s}} crew was composed of the elite, a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] personally selected by the Supreme Commander,<ref name="kenner" /> [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader himself.<ref name="TFUd" /> A wide variety of stormtrooper classes protected the ship, including [[Shadow stormtrooper/Legends|Shadow Troopers]], [[purge trooper]]s, and even the hazardous-environment EVO troopers.<ref name="TFUg" /> A number of [[Interrogation droid/Legends|interrogation droids]] were also used aboard the vessel to watch and control troublesome alien subjects. The vessel's complement of soldiers was trained to quickly handle threats that broke out aboard the ship, and they would take any measures to prevent test subjects from escaping alive.<ref name="TFUd" /> The [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] also had control of the ship's self-destruct, which he could use to exterminate everyone aboard if necessary.<ref name="TFUn" /> The entire crew and vessel were disposable to Vader; he would ultimately order all their deaths to conceal the survival of his apprentice, Galen Marek.<ref name="TFUc" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:EmpiricalBridgeConcept.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Early concept art of the ''Empirical''{{'s}} bridge, by [[Chin Ko]].]]
The ''Empirical'' was created for the [[2008]] multimedia project ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', and appears in all adaptations of ''The Force Unleashed''{{'s}} story. The ''Empirical'' is a level of the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|video game]] for the [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]]; for the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]], [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 2|PlayStation 2]], and all other versions produced by [[Krome Studios]], the events on the ''Empirical'' occur in a cutscene. In the Xbox/PlayStation version, the room where Marek first awakens has monitors on which the name of [[Lucasfilm]] employee [[Victor Tancredi-Ballugera]] is written in [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]].

In the PS3/Xbox 360 versions of the game, stormtroopers mention that Galen Marek's code name on the ship is 'Subject 1138', which is a reference to George Lucas' first film, [[1138 (easter egg)|''THX-1138'']].

Despite all adaptations of ''The Force Unleashed'' telling the same story, the events, and even the layout, of the ''Empirical'' change between them. In both the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|novel]] and [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|comic]], PROXY joins Marek as he travels through the ship; in the game, he leaves for the ''Rogue Shadow'' and meets Marek there. Different aspects of the ship's design also vary between adaptations. For instance, the exterior views shown in the comic and game differ greatly. Similarly, in the game, Juno Eclipse's cell is located in an area that looks like the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of the vessel; however, in the comic, it looks very different.

The interior design of the ''Empirical'' was inspired by the sterile, military feel of Imperial facilities shown in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' films. The room Marek awakens in, called "Vader's Laboratory," is reminiscent of the lab in the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center|EmPal SuRecon Center]], where Darth Vader's body is reconstructed in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]. The general tone of the ''Empirical'' level in the game was meant to evoke a sense of foreboding and dread for the player.<ref name="Art and Making">''[[The Art and Making of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>
